summary: Added a Modbus/SunSpec driver foundation for myiotsan's planned solar-system support (P5), plus a standalone simulator to develop and prove it without real hardware. `infra/iot/sunspec` decodes the SunSpec information model that rides on Modbus: it walks a device's self-describing model chain (Common/Inverter/Meter/Storage/Controls), applies each field's scale-factor arithmetic, and role-prefixes every emitted key (`inv_ac_power`, `grid_ac_power`, `batt_soc`, `ctl_w_max_lim_pct`) so a hybrid inverter's own inverter block and its built-in grid meter never collide -- one driver decodes any compliant inverter/meter/battery with no per-vendor register map. `infra/iot/modbus` adds a stdlib Modbus TCP client (read holding/input, write single/multiple), a `RegisterMap` for the many cheaper, non-SunSpec-compliant devices that expose a flat vendor register block instead, a `Poller` that normalises either path to the same `codec.Sample` shape the MQTT ingest path already produces, and a guarded `WriteConfirm` that writes a register then confirms by read-back and never re-issues the write -- a Modbus write to an inverter or battery is a physical action, so a lost confirmation must not become a second one, mirroring the rule already enforced on the MQTT actuation path. `tools/sunspec-sim` is a new stdlib SunSpec-over-Modbus-TCP simulator serving three devices on three Modbus unit ids (a SunSpec hybrid inverter, a standalone SunSpec meter, and a non-SunSpec vendor inverter) driven by a live physics loop (PV bell curve, battery charge/discharge, grid balance, curtailment), so the mixed-protocol case a real solar system presents can be developed and tested without hardware; its control registers are honoured so a guarded write's read-back genuinely changes. Verified live: the driver read all three simulated personas and confirmed a curtailment write by read-back over a real Modbus TCP connection, in addition to hermetic unit tests covering the decoding and scaling deterministically. This is design and driver foundation only -- no app wiring: `device_profile`/`telemetry_key` still only understand a JSON-path binding, nothing in `app.go` polls Modbus yet, and the solar "system workspace" that would group an inverter+battery+meters into one monitored system (P8) remains design-only. See `docs/MYIOTSAN_PLAN.md` section 8g.
compatibility: No behavior change for any running myiotsan install: the new code is not called from `app.go`, ships no new config keys, and adds no new listening port or dependency beyond the Go standard library (no third-party Modbus package). `tools/sunspec-sim` is developer-only tooling with no runtime dependency on `apps/`, `domain/`, or `infra/`, and is never bundled into a myiotsan release. Existing devices, profiles, and rules are entirely unaffected until the app-integration follow-up (P5) lands.
